"i.

That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash the impugned notice dated 8.1.2018 (Annexure -P/1) issued by the respondent No.3.

That, any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper may also kindly be granted to the petitioner in the interest of justice along with costs of the petition."
2.
Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner was running a bottle godown in a rented premises.
The godown was taken on rent from respondent No.4 in the year 1981, in which, he was continuously doing his business.
In other portion of the land owned by respondent No.4, he constructed Pithaliya Complex.
In between Pithaliya complex constructed by respondent No.4 and rented premises possessed by petitioner of respondent No.4 there is a road.
Respondent No.3 issued notice to petitioner in collusion with respondent No.4, who some how wants to get the vacant possession of the godown.
Respondent No.3 has given only 24 hours to vacate the premises/godown.

He contended that in the notice issued by respondent No.2 there is mention that the shop operated/constructed by petitioner, which is sought to be evicted, is coming under the proposed road widening identified by the department.
If the land on which godown is constructed is needed for widening of the road, the respondent No.3 ought to have acquired the said portion of the land according to the provisions of law.

The petitioner ought to have been issued a show cause notice specifying the portion of the premises to be affected by the required road widening and further respondent No.3 ought to have acted in a fair manner providing sufficient breathing time to petitioner to vacate the premises.
He contended that the building constructed by respondent No.4 in the corner of the road ought not to have been demolished as in front of the premises of petitioner there is sufficient open land.
Petitioner has not encroached upon any of the portion of the government land.
He submits that in the notice it is not mentioned as to how much area respondent-corporation needs for widening of the road and therefore, notice is vague.

3. Learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 3 submits that in reply to the writ petition, it has been specifically pleaded that the premises on which the bottle godown is being run by petitioner is owned by Kishore Bhai and Kailash Pithaliya.
Initially notices have been given to them on 06.05.2015, 01.10.2015, 24.11.2016 and lastly on 06.01.2018.

In the said notice, there is specific mention that widening of the road from K.K. Road to Station Rod has to be done and their land/building is coming within the widening of the road and therefore, they may approach with relevant documents of ownership and building permission.

He contended that Kishore Chand and Kailash Chand Pithaliya replied the notice dated 06.01.2018 stating that on the land, subject matter of writ petition, they are having two tenants and they have informed them on 06.01.2018 to vacate the premises.
They have also given no objection for use of their land and for removing construction over the land by Municipal Corporation in the public interest reserving right to initiate proceedings.
Copies of the letter is placed on record along with reply.
He also submits that copies of the letters sent by respondent No.4 to both the tenants including petitioner asking them to vacate the rented premises with receipt thereof are also placed on record.
In view of the letter written by respondent No.4, petitioner is served with notice for removing the article kept in the premises which are the scrap bottles.
Petitioner being the tenant and consent being given by the land owners is not having any locus to file this petition.
In support of his contention, he placed reliance upon the decision in case of Municipal Corporation Raipur Vs. Bhushan Lal Sahu, reported in 2011 (2) CGLJ 134.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for respondent No.4 vehemently opposes the submission of learned counsel for petitioner and would submit that petitioner is not the owner of the land/premises on which he is running business.
Respondent No.4 is the owner of property, subject matter of writ petition, which was needed by respondents No.2 and 3 for widening of the road.
Notices were issued to respondent No.4 and lastly respondent No.4 gave his consent in public interest for use of his land/premises for construction and widening of the road.
He submits that petitioner by way of rejoinder is claiming compensation.
Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation of land or building.

He was given prior notice for removal of the goods from the godown and further the estimate amount placed in record for construction of new building over the land recorded in the name of respondent No.4,
shows the intention of petitioner to some how grab the property and therefore, the writ petition is filed on fictitious grounds.

5. Learned counsel for State submits that pursuant to the direction issued by this Court reply has been filed mentioning that action is taken by respondents No.2 and 3 under the provisions of Section 322 (3) of the Chhattisgarh Municipal Corporation Act, 1956.
The State Government issued circular dated 19.01.2018 to follow the legal formalities in case of action to be taken under the aforementioned provisions.
He submits that as per the order passed by this Court, status-quo with respect to the property in question has been made and it is covered by fences.
On 09.01.2018 when case was listed for hearing, learned counsel for Municipal Corporation had made submission on instruction that godown in question has already been demolished.
6. In reply, learned counsel for petitioner submits that in the notice there is no specific mention of khasra number or plot number etc.

It is contended that looking to the strict view taken by the High Court, the Secretary, Urban Administration Department, State of Chhattisgarh and Commissioner,
Municipal Corporation, Raipur present before this Court, made submissions that the action like present taken will not be repeated in future.

No objection given by respondent No.4 for using his land and for demolition of premises erected over it does not bear receiving seal and signature of Municipal Corporation and respondent No.4 has not admitted to the letter dated 06.01.2018 in the reply.

It is further contended that respondent No.2 and 3 has not made any application for vacating of stay order for the purpose of widening of the road, in fact the encroachment is made on the other side of the road by constructing building, by respondent No.4.

He contended that as the building possessed by petitioner was demolished, respondent No.2 and 3 ought to pay the amount of Rs.22,17,100/- for construction of the bottle godown and residential house of petitioner.
7. I have heard learned counsel for petitioner and perused the documents placed on record.

8. Perusal of the pleadings made in the writ petition itself would show that petitioner in categorical terms pleaded that petitioner is running bottle godown upon the rented premises which he got on rent from respondent No.4.
He is paying continuously rent from January, 1981 without any fail and is operating his business.

During the course of arguments also, when this Court posed specific query as to whether he took the land on rent/lease or the entire building premises over the land to which learned counsel for petitioner fairly submitted that the premises constructed by respondent No.4 was taken on rent.
From the pleadings and the submission made by learned counsel for petitioner it is apparent that petitioner was not the owner of the land or building.

sentences.text: it is appearing that respondents No.2 and 3 issued multiple notices to respondent No.4 to produce the details of construction/ownership of the land as the said property is coming within the widening of the road.
First notice which is placed in record is dated 06.05.2015.
Other notices are dated 01.10.2015, 24.11.2016 and 06.01.2018.
No objection issued by Kishore Chand and Kailash Chand Pithaliya is also placed on record along with reply filed by respondents No.2 and 3.

Perusal of the same would show that respondent No.4 gave no objection with respect to use of his land for the public purpose for construction of road and if construction is removed by Municipal Corporation, Raipur he is having no objection.

In the right hand corner it is the signature of the officials, who received the letter/No objection and therefore,
submission of learned counsel for petitioner that no objection written by respondent No.4 does not bear the receipt seal is not acceptable, more so when this document is filed by respondents No.2 and 3 to whom the said document was addressed by respondent No.4.
9.

Learned counsel for respondent No.4 during the course of argument before this Court has made specific statement that respondent No.4 had issued no objection to the Municipal Corporation and petitioner has no locus to file this petition as he is not the owner of the property.

In view of the submission made by learned counsel for respondent No.4, submission of learned counsel for petitioner that the property, subject matter owned by respondent No.4, to which he took on rent, the submission that respondent No.4 has not given any no objection to respondent No.2 and 3 is also not sustainable.
10. Perusal of the order sheets dated 09.01.2018 would show that pursuant to the notice dated 08.01.2018, the construction of the godown which is subject mater of writ petition has already been demolished, before this petition was taken up for hearing.
In the entire petition, or in the rejoinder filed to the return of respondents No.2 and 3, petitioner has not pleaded as to what loss he suffered of the scrap bottles, if any, kept in the godown.
In fact in the rejoinder, petitioner has claimed Rs.22,00,000/- for construction of building based on the estimate prepared by Rao and Rao Associates.

The said estimate is for the purpose of construction of new building of ground floor,
mazananine floor, parafit wall and stair case tower.

11. Admittedly the building which was demolished and land over which the godown/building was standing is not owned by petitioner and therefore, petitioner can not claim any damages for the building which is already demolished or the land to be used by the respondent No.2 and 3 for public purpose subject to the rights of the registered owner of the property.

12. In case of Municipal Corporation Vs. Bhushan Lal Sahu (supra), this Court has held as under :-
"14.

sentences.text: Definitions of words or connotations are internal aids to construction.

In The Vanguard Fire and General Insurance Co. Ltd., Madras v. Fraser and Ross, AIR 1960 SC 971, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that when a word has been defined in the interpretation clause prima facie, that definition governs whenever that word is used in the body of the Statute.

sentences.text:
In Wyre Forest District Council v. Secretary of State for the Environment, (1990) 1 All ER 780 (785), Lord Lowry has held thus :
" ..............if Parliament in a statutory enactment defines its terms (whether by enlarging or by restricting the ordinary meaning of a word or expression), it must intend that, in the absence of a clear indication to the contrary, those terms as defined shall govern what is proposed, authorised or done under or by reference to that enactment..........."

entities.text: Wyre Forest District Council v. Secretary of State for the Environment, (1990) 1 All ER 780 (785)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 5 of the Act begins with the words 'in this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context to indicate that in the absence of any repugnancy in the subject or context the definition or the meaning assigned to each of the words defined in the Act shall cany its meaning through out the Statute as has been defined.

On scrutiny of the provisions contained in Sections 305 and 306 of the Act, it does not appear that there is anything repugnant in the subject or context in which the word 'owner' has been used in the said provisions.

Thus, this Court has no hesitation in holding that a tenant would not be covered within the sweep and ambit of Sections 305, 306 and 387 of the Act so as to be entitled to compensation in the event the land or building belonging to its owner/landlord is acquired by the Corporation.
15. The above view of this Court is also supported by observation made in a Division Bench judgment of this Court in Municipal Corporation, Raipur v. Smt. Mandakini Ram (supra).

entities.text: Municipal Corporation, Raipur v. Smt. Mandakini Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In paragraph 8 of the report, the Division Bench has observed that 'in such vesting, the Corporation shall make reasonable compensation to the 'owner' for any damage or loss he may sustain in consequence of his building or any part thereof being set back'.

In the later part of paragraph 8, the Division Bench has further observed that 'the only right which can be claimed against the Corporation under this Act on such vesting is the right of reasonable compensation which can be claimed by the owner of the land only'.

16. Learned counsel for the respondent has argued that in the absence of any notification under Section 305 of the Act, it cannot be said that there was widening of the public street as defined under Section 5(49) of the Act, therefore, Sections 305 and 306 of the Act have no application.

This argument of learned counsel for the respondent has no legal backing and in fact is no longer res integra in view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in The Municipal Corporation, Indore v. K.N. Palsikar, AIR 1969 SC 579 in which the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in paragraph 14 of the report, has held thus :
"14. Regarding point No. 1

entities.text: Municipal Corporation, Indore v. K.N. Palsikar, AIR 1969 SC 579
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , we agree with the High Court that there is no provision in the Act for enabling the Corporation to withdraw from the acquisition proceedings.
In fact, it seems to us that there is automatic vesting of the land in the Corporation under Section 305 once the requisite conditions are satisfied.............."

In view of what has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in The Municipal Corporation, Indore v. K.N. Palsikar (supra), more particularly in view of the observation made by the learned District Judge in paragraph 2 of the impugned order, referring to Gazette notifications dated 18-4-2001 and Saleh Mohammad vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83988335/
5 15-9-2006, this Court is of the opinion that the provisions of Sections 305, 306 and 387 of the Act are applicable in the present case qua the 'owner'."
13.

sentences.text: In the aforementioned facts of the case, when notice of demolition has already been executed and building has been demolished, no relief can be granted to petitioner.
Similarly the compensation of Rs.22,00,000/- as claimed by petitioner for construction of new building also cannot be granted in view of the discussions made here-in-above.
14. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.

However, taking note of the fact that notice was issued for removing construction on 08.01.2018 giving only 24 hours time to be arbitrary, which has caused mental pain and agony to petitioner, respondent No.2 and 3 are directed to pay petitioner a sum of Rs.25,000/- as compensation for the pain and agony suffered by petitioner by their arbitrary acts.
